footprint.notes: Lilly's FY2024 10-K names production states and countries without figures (major production sites in Indiana, North Carolina, Puerto Rico and New Jersey; Ireland, France, Spain, Italy, China and Japan) and says approximately 25,000 of about 47,000 employees are outside the U.S.; the U.S. remainder is not stated, so it is not derived. Investment figures come from Lilly's press releases at lilly.mediaroom.com (the press-release host linked from lilly.com/news/press-releases) and a lilly.com story. Lilly states state-wide totals only for North Carolina (roughly $4 billion since 2020, as of January 2023), Wisconsin ($4 billion total planned, December 2024) and Indiana (more than $21 billion since 2020, as of May 2026). Before 2026, Indiana had only site-level figures (Lebanon LEAP district more than $13 billion by October 2024; $1.2 billion to update Indianapolis facilities, May 2024). The three state values come from different dates, are not a common snapshot, and were not summed or adjusted. After the FY2024 snapshot, Lilly's press-release index lists further U.S. sites: Virginia ($5 billion) and Texas ($6.5 billion) in September 2025, Puerto Rico (more than $1.2 billion) in October 2025, Alabama ($6 billion) in December 2025, and Pennsylvania's Lehigh Valley, selected in January 2026 with $3.5 billion stated at its November 2026 groundbreaking. These are not recorded as sites or state values because they fall after the snapshot; Lilly has not published a state-wide total for those states. The February 26, 2025 release reports $50 billion of U.S. capital commitments since 2020, with no per-state split.
